title: Pralhad Joshi takes charge as Union education minister, vows to work with 'humility and honesty'
content:
led protest at Delhi's Jantar Mantar. In his first reaction since assuming the charge, Joshi thanked Prime Minister Narendra Modi for reposing faith in him and pledging to discharge his responsibilities with "humility and honesty".
President Droupadi Murmu accepted Pradhan's resignation from the Union Council of Ministers with immediate effect. Joshi, who currently holds the portfolios of Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution, and New and Renewable Energy, has been entrusted with the Education Ministry in addition to his existing responsibilities.
"I thank the Prime Minister for giving such a huge responsibility and with great trust he has assigned this responsibility to me. Under his guidance and leadership, I will perform this responsibility with full strength, humility and honesty," Joshi told PTI.
Quick answers to key questions
Pralhad Joshi is the Union Minister who has taken additional charge of the Ministry of Education following the resignation of Dharmendra Pradhan. He is also responsible for other portfolios such as Consumer Affairs and Renewable Energy.
led protest over alleged NEET-UG examination irregularities, which lasted for 37 days and called for accountability in the education system.
The government has agreed to discuss key demands from the Cockroach Janta Party, including the withdrawal of FIRs against protesters and the implementation of a five-point charter for examination reforms.
The protest concluded after the resignation of Dharmendra Pradhan and assurances from the government regarding addressing the protesters' demands, leading the Cockroach Janta Party to withdraw in good faith.
Pralhad Joshi emphasized a commitment to humility and honesty in addressing his responsibilities, indicating a focus on accountability and transparency in the education sector as demanded by the youth.
Joshi's appointment came after the Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) withdrew its 37-day agitation at Jantar Mantar following assurances from the Centre on key demands linked to alleged NEET-UG examination irregularities.
Reacting to the appointment, CJP chief spokesperson Saurav Das said the organisation would soon meet the new education minister and urged him to implement its five-point charter on examination reforms.
"Our concerns and demands have been addressed. Whoever becomes the Education Minister should know that the youth are watching. They will demand accountability. Work in the interest of the youth, stop paper leaks and implement our five-point recommendations," Das told ANI.
He said the Centre had assured the organisation that another round of talks would be held within a month to discuss the reform agenda.
Das also said the CJP would initiate legal action against Delhi Police and Rapid Action Force personnel accused of using excessive force during the July 20 protests. He, however, described the organisation's meeting with Delhi Police Commissioner Anurag Kumar as "cordial".
CJP national spokesperson Ashutosh Ranka also welcomed Joshi's appointment, calling the outcome of the agitation a victory for democratic accountability.
Following the withdrawal of the protest, authorities restored mobile internet services around Jantar Mantar, while the Delhi Metro Rail Corporation resumed normal operations across its network after days of security-related restrictions.
The CJP ended its agitation after the third round of talks with Union ministers J P Nadda and Jitendra Singh, saying it accepted the government's assurances in "good faith" and expected the commitments to be implemented within the agreed timelines.

title: From Smriti Irani to Pralhad Joshi: 12 years, 5 Education Ministers under NDA—a look at their tenures as Pradhan resigns
content:
Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan resigned on Saturday, taking moral responsibility amid the NEET-UG 2026 paper leak controversy after weeks of nationwide protests led by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP). His resignation came after a 37-day agitation that demanded accountability for examination irregularities and reforms in the education system. Soon after, Prahlad Joshi was given additional charge of the Ministry of Education while continuing as Union Minister for Consumer Affairs. time education minister to serve under Prime Minister Narendra Modi since the NDA came to power in 2014. Over the past 12 years, the ministry has overseen the rollout of the National Education Policy (NEP) 2020, curriculum changes, digital learning initiatives, while also facing controversies over paper leaks, board examinations and entrance tests. Quick answers to key questions UG 2026 paper leak controversy, taking moral responsibility for examination irregularities after a prolonged agitation demanding accountability and education reforms. Since 2014, the NDA has seen five Education Ministers, including Smriti Irani and Dharmendra Pradhan, each focusing on various initiatives like the National Education Policy, digital learning, and addressing examination controversies. The NEP 2020 was significant as it replaced the 34-year-old National Policy on Education from 1986, marking a major shift in India's education framework and was approved during Ramesh Pokhriyal's time as Education Minister. Student protests highlighted the discontent over the NEET paper leak, leading to significant governmental actions, including reprimanding officials of the National Testing Agency and prompting accountability measures from the Education Ministry. During his tenure, Dharmendra Pradhan focused on implementing the NEP 2020, promoting digital education, enhancing skill-based learning, and reforming national entrance examinations amid challenges like paper leak controversies. When the BJP formed its first government in May 2014, Smriti Irani was appointed Minister of Human Resource Development (HRD), becoming one of the youngest leaders to hold the portfolio. Her tenure focused on expanding higher education access, strengthening skill development and implementing digital initiatives in schools and universities. However, it was also marked by political controversies surrounding appointments at central universities, debates over academic freedom, and the Rohith Vemula and JNU episodes, which dominated national discourse. In July 2016, she was shifted to the Textiles Ministry during the first major Cabinet reshuffle under the Modi government. Prakash Javadekar succeeded Irani in July 2016 and remained HRD Minister until the end of the Modi government's first term. His tenure focused on improving school learning outcomes, promoting digital education platforms such as SWAYAM, expanding online teacher training, and streamlining higher education regulations. The government also accelerated work on drafting a new National Education Policy during this period. The CBSE was hit by a major paper leak controversy in March 2018 involving the Class 10 Mathematics and Class 12 Economics board examinations. After reports that both question papers had been circulated on WhatsApp before the exams, CBSE announced a nationwide re-examination for the Class 12 Economics paper. exam for Class 10 Mathematics but later withdrew the decision after determining that the leak's impact was limited and did not warrant a nationwide retest. Javadekar was replaced after the BJP returned to power with a larger mandate in the 2019 Lok Sabha elections. Former Uttarakhand Chief Minister Ramesh Pokhriyal took charge in May 2019, initially as HRD Minister. His tenure is remembered primarily for two landmark developments. In July 2020, the Union Cabinet approved the National Education Policy (NEP) 2020, replacing the 34-year-old National Policy on Education of 1986. The ministry was simultaneously renamed from the Ministry of Human Resource Development to the Ministry of Education, restoring its pre-1985 name. 19 pandemic, overseeing online classes, revised CBSE examinations and digital learning initiatives. He resigned during the July 2021 Cabinet reshuffle. Dharmendra Pradhan assumed office in July 2021 following the Cabinet reshuffle. year tenure, the ministry concentrated on implementing NEP 2020, introducing changes to the National Curriculum Framework, strengthening multilingual education, promoting skill-based learning, expanding digital education and reforming national entrance examinations. However, his final years in office were overshadowed by repeated controversies involving competitive examinations, which started with the NEET-UG and UGC-NET examinations in 2024, when allegations of question paper leaks and compromised exam integrity prompted the Centre to cancel the UGC-NET exam, order a CBI probe and announce reforms in the NTA's functioning. In 2026, fresh controversies erupted after the NEET-UG paper leak led to the cancellation of the examination, termination of 47 NTA officials and criminal proceedings against those allegedly involved. Soon after, allegations of a UGC-NET 2026 paper leak further intensified criticism of the ministry, with opposition parties demanding accountability and reforms in the examination system. Following Pradhan's resignation, senior BJP leader Pralhad Joshi was entrusted with additional charge of the Education Ministry while retaining the Consumer Affairs portfolio. title: Pralhad Joshi gets additional charge of Education Ministry after Dharmendra Pradhan resigns- Who is he?
content:
time Dharwad MP Pralhad Joshi has been assigned charge of the education ministry, in addition to his existing portfolio. The move comes hours after Dharmendra Pradhan resigned after mass Cockroach Janta Party (CJP)-led protests over NEET paper leak.
President Droupadi Murmu, as advised by the Prime Minister Narendra Modi, has accepted the resignation of Dharmendra Pradhan from the Union Council of Ministers, a press release by the government says.
He currently serves as the Union Minister of Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution, and New and Renewable Energy (MNRE).
Quick answers to key questions
Pralhad Joshi was assigned the additional charge of the Education Ministry following Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation amidst mass protests over a NEET paper leak.
Pralhad Joshi currently serves as the Union Minister for Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution, and New and Renewable Energy, alongside his new role in the Education Ministry.
As Minister for New and Renewable Energy, Joshi has implemented initiatives aimed at increasing renewable energy capacity and reducing fossil fuel reliance, including the National Green Hydrogen Mission.
Dharmendra Pradhan resigned due to intense nationwide protests led by the Cockroach Janta Party over allegations of irregularities in the NEET examination.
Yes, as the new Education Minister, Pralhad Joshi should prioritize accountability and reforms related to the NEET paper leak and related issues to restore trust in the education system.
In an official statement, the government confirmed the change in ministerial responsibilities.
"President Droupadi Murmu, as advised by the Prime Minister, has accepted the resignation of Dharmendra Pradhan from the Union Council of Ministers," the government said in a press release.
The statement further announced that, on the Prime Minister's advice, Joshi had been entrusted with the additional charge of the Ministry of Education alongside his current responsibilities.
Pradhan's exit follows weeks of nationwide protests led by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) over the alleged NEET paper leak, with the issue becoming one of the most politically sensitive controversies confronting the Centre.
Pralhad Joshi is a senior Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) leader from Karnataka and a five-time Lok Sabha MP representing the Dharwad constituency. Widely regarded as one of the party's experienced parliamentarians, he has handled several key ministries during his political career.
Before taking charge of the Education Ministry, Joshi served as the Union Minister for Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution and the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE). In the previous Modi government, he held the portfolios of Coal, Mines and Parliamentary Affairs.
His parliamentary experience spans five consecutive terms from Dharwad, making him one of the BJP's longest-serving MPs from Karnataka.
As Minister for New and Renewable Energy, Joshi has been responsible for implementing several flagship initiatives aimed at accelerating India's clean energy transition and meeting the country's long-term climate commitments.
The ministry is steering efforts to achieve 500 GW of renewable and non-fossil fuel-based power capacity by 2030 and the national target of net zero emissions by 2070.
Under his leadership, the ministry has pursued measures including annual bids for 50 GW of renewable energy projects until 2027, waivers on Inter-State Transmission System (ISTS) charges, expansion of Renewable Purchase Obligations (RPOs), development of large renewable energy parks, and viability gap funding for offshore wind projects.
Pralhad Joshi has also overseen major programmes such as the National Green Hydrogen Mission and the PM Surya Ghar initiative, both central to the government's strategy for expanding clean energy adoption and reducing dependence on fossil fuels.

title: Dharmendra Pradhan resigns, FIRs withdrawn, compensation promised: CJP ends protest
content:
The Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) announced on Saturday (25 July) that it was withdrawing its month-long agitation over the alleged NEET paper leak, after Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan resigned and they secured government commitments on compensation for affected families and the withdrawal of criminal cases filed against protesters.
Announcing the outcome of talks with the government, CJP Chief Spokesperson Saurav Das said the outfit was calling off its protest on the understanding that promises made would be honoured on schedule. "Cockroach Janta Party declares that we withdraw the agitation in good faith, with the understanding that the agreed-upon terms will be executed within the agreed-upon timelines," Das said.
The announcement caps a campaign that began at Jantar Mantar on 20 June and had already claimed Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation earlier in the day, a development the group had described as the movement's first victory.
Quick answers to key questions
The CJP's protest was primarily driven by demands for accountability over the NEET paper leak controversy, which they believed jeopardized the futures of numerous students. Their key demands included Pradhan's resignation, compensation for families affected by the issue, and the withdrawal of legal cases against protesters.
The government has committed to providing ₹1 crore as compensation to the families of NEET victims, responding to one of the primary demands made by the Cockroach Janata Party.
The CJP stipulated that their retreat from the protest was contingent upon the government honoring its commitments, including timely payment of compensation and the withdrawal of FIRs against protesters.
The government agreed to withdraw all FIRs filed against protesters, a demand put forth by the CJP, and assured that the process would proceed quickly and transparently.
The CJP indicated they would remain vigilant regarding the government's fulfillment of agreed promises and planned to engage in further talks about educational reforms within a month following the protest's conclusion.
National Spokesperson Ashutosh Ranka set out the financial commitment secured from the government, one of the CJP's founding demands. "We had demanded compensation of ₹1 crore for the families of NEET victims. The government has agreed to this, stating that an honorary compensation will be given to those families under whatever rules and regulations allow," Ranka said.
Ranka added that the discussions had extended well beyond compensation, touching on a wider agenda for reform that the CJP intends to pursue in further engagement with the government.
"Apart from this, we also placed a five-point demand charter before the government, which talked about broader educational reforms and exam reforms. We will meet the government again in about four weeks regarding that demand charter so that we can work together on broader reforms," he said, adding that the agitation's continued withdrawal was contingent on the government following through. "If all these demands are agreeable to the government, then we would also like to withdraw the agitation."
Das also detailed progress on the CJP's second core demand, concerning the legal cases filed against demonstrators during the protest. "Our second demand was that all the FIRs filed against the protesters, not just in Delhi but in all BJP-ruled and BJP-allied states, should be withdrawn. This was also our second demand. The government has accepted that demand as well," he said.
According to Das, officials have given assurances that the process will move quickly and transparently. "Furthermore, the withdrawal will be done shortly. The government has assured us that it will share copies of all the FIRs filed, as per our last information, 15 to 20 FIRs were filed in Delhi, and we will receive those copies within three to four days in any case. The government has also assured that the withdrawal will be done shortly," he said.
To formalise the understanding reached in talks, the CJP said it had submitted its own draft assurance to the government for sign-off. "Understanding this, we have shared a draft with the government, which is a written guarantee. The government has said it will share this with us by Tuesday. We hope that by Tuesday we will receive the government's guarantees regarding these FIRs and any future action," Das said.
The withdrawal brings a formal close, for now, to a 36-day agitation that had drawn thousands to Jantar Mantar, featured a prolonged hunger strike by environmentalist Sonam Wangchuk, and culminated in Pradhan's resignation earlier on Saturday.
With compensation pledged, FIR withdrawals promised, and a fresh round of talks scheduled within a month over broader examination and education reforms, the CJP has signalled that its retreat from the streets is conditional rather than final, with the group keeping a close watch on whether the government's assurances are honoured within the stated timelines.

title: Time has come to remove this govt: Rahul Gandhi harks 'don't be afraid!' as Dharmendra Pradhan resigns
content:
Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha and Congress leader Rahul Gandhi has reacted to Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation. “Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation is a huge step towards reshaping our education system. Well done to students across the country; we are proud of all of you.”, Rahul Gandhi said on Saturday (25 July). “Heartiest congratulations to every young person, every student who took to the streets and stood firm to protect democracy, the Constitution, and their future.” The Congress MP added. The Amethi MP, being a a touchstone, reminded, “2 demands still remain - the Prime Minister should apologize while respecting the students and India's future, and action should be taken against those guilty of violence against students.” Quick answers to key questions Dharmendra Pradhan resigned to address student protests over alleged irregularities in competitive examinations and to prevent the situation from being exploited by 'anti-national forces.' Rahul Gandhi hailed the resignation as a significant step towards reforming the education system, expressing pride in the students for standing firm in defense of democracy and their future. Students demand an apology from the Prime Minister for the government's actions against them and accountability for police brutality during protests, alongside broader reforms in the education system. The Congress party celebrated the resignation as a victory for the youth of India, claiming it demonstrated the power of student activism and their push for accountability in the education sector. Rahul Gandhi emphasized that while Pradhan's resignation is a victory, the broader fight for justice and reform for students continues, noting that the Prime Minister's apology and action against police responsible for violence are still needed. "For other sections of society—farmers, laborers, the poor, every person whom this government has suppressed and crushed—true courage lies in standing firm in a constitutional manner for one's dignity. The time has come to remove this government." Rahul Gandhi posted on X (formerly Twitter) Dharmendra Pradhan announced his resignation on Saturday (25 July), saying he had submitted it to Prime Minister Narendra Modi in the interest of students and to ensure that the ongoing protests over examination irregularities were not exploited by "anti-national forces." The resignation follows weeks of nationwide protests over alleged irregularities in competitive examinations, with students demanding greater transparency, accountability, and reforms in the examination system. The Indian National Congress moved swiftly to claim the moment as vindication of its own campaign, describing the resignation as a defining win for the country's younger generation. In a post on its official X account, the party wrote, “Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation is a victory for the youth, a victory for India's Gen Z. This victory belongs to those millions of young people who raised their voices across the country to fix the education system. In the face of the youth's truth, Narendra Modi's arrogance has been shattered, and his lies have been defeated.” The party credited Gandhi with keeping the paper leak issue alive since it first surfaced, tracing his advocacy from public demonstrations through to Parliament. "The youth have forced an incompetent and corrupt Education Minister, Dharmendra Pradhan, to resign. From the very first day of the NEET paper leak, opposition leader Rahul Gandhi and the Congress Party have been fighting, from the streets to Parliament, to deliver justice to the youth. This fight will continue, until the education system is reformed," the party said. Congress also renewed its demand for an apology over the police response to demonstrators at Jantar Mantar on 20 July. "Narendra Modi will have to apologise for ordering lathis to be used on our youth and for the attacks with pellet guns," the post read. The party's youth wing, the Indian Youth Congress, echoed the sentiment that Pradhan's exit marked only an opening success rather than a conclusion. IYC president Uday Bhanu Chib credited sustained student pressure and Gandhi's continued advocacy for the outcome. "This is the first victory of the country's youth and students' struggle. Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation is the power of the youth's voice," Chib said. He was, however, unambiguous that the movement's broader objectives remained unmet. "Pradhan's resignation is a handful of dust in the eyes. Until the prime minister apologises to the country's youth, Amit Shah resigns for ordering the lathi charge on students, and action is taken against the responsible police officers, this Gen Z movement will not be victorious," Chib said. The move follows weeks of nationwide demonstrations over alleged irregularities in competitive examinations, with students demanding greater transparency, accountability and root and branch reform of the examination system. title: RBI, govt measures could turn India's balance of payments surplus, ease pressure on rupee: HDFC
content:
New Delhi [India]: India's balance of payments (BoP) could return to a small surplus instead of recording a third consecutive annual deficit following a series of measures announced by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) and the government in June, according to HDFC Mutual Fund's July report.
The report said the measures could ease pressure on the rupee by improving capital inflows and strengthening the country's external position.
"The RBI and government's June measures could turn what could have been a third straight year of balance-of-payments deficit into a small surplus, thereby taking pressure off the rupee," the report said.
According to the report, the RBI's decision to bear the full hedging cost for fresh three-to-five-year FCNR(B) deposits until September 30, 2026, could attract potential inflows of USD 40-60 billion. It added that around USD 17 billion had already been mobilised under this route as of July 17, 2026.
The report also said the concessional foreign exchange swap facility for external commercial borrowings by public sector undertakings could attract another USD 15-25 billion in inflows while reducing hedging costs. It added that the expansion of the Fully Accessible Route (FAR) for government securities and the removal of foreign portfolio investment limits on short-term investments would improve the flexibility and accessibility of investments in Indian government bonds.
Further, the report noted that the government's decision to withdraw capital gains and withholding tax on returns from investments in government securities increases the likelihood of Indian bonds being included in the Bloomberg bond index at its next review. Such inclusion could potentially attract USD 10-20 billion over the next 12-18 months, it added.
The report said the depreciation of the rupee over the past 12-18 months has been driven largely by weaker capital flows rather than weak economic fundamentals. It noted that, in real trade-weighted terms, the rupee was at its most undervalued level since the 2013 taper tantrum as of May 2026.
Looking ahead, HDFC Mutual Fund said the recent policy measures have the potential to strengthen India's external sector by supporting capital inflows, improving the balance of payments and reducing pressure on the rupee.

title: Isuzu signs five-year pact with Kamarajar Port for vehicle exports
content:
Isuzu Motors India Pvt. Ltd., a subsidiary of the Japanese auto major Isuzu, has signed a five-year agreement with Kamarajar Port Ltd (KPL) for the export of commercial vehicles through the port’s General Cargo Berth. This strengthens the partnership between the two that has been in place since 2019.
Under the agreement, Isuzu Motors India will receive concessional wharfage rates linked to export volumes for the next five years, a move aimed at enhancing the competitiveness of vehicle exports through the port.
Isuzu’s manufacturing facility at Sri City in Andhra Pradesh has been exporting its D-Max and S-Cab models through Kamarajar Port to key West Asia markets, including Saudi Arabia, Qatar, Kuwait, Oman and Jordan, since 2019.
The agreement was signed by Hironori Okawa, Assistant General Manager, Isuzu Motors India, and Thirumurugan, General Manager (Operations), Kamarajar Port, in the presence of JP Irene Cynthia, Managing Director of Kamarajar Port, and senior officials from both organisations.
Kamarajar Port in a social media post said the agreement reinforces its commitment to providing efficient, customer-centric and globally competitive port services while further strengthening its position as a preferred gateway for automobile exports.
Rajesh Mittal, President and Managing Director of Isuzu Motors India, told businessline that the port has played a significant role in strengthening the company’s export operations over the past few years.
“We are happy to continue our strategic partnership with Kamarajar Port Ltd, which has played a significant role in strengthening our export operations over the last few years. This long-term collaboration is an important enabler for us to be among the leading commercial vehicle exporters in our category,” he said.
Mittal said the company remains committed to its “Make in India, for India and the globe” strategy by manufacturing world-class vehicles in India for domestic and overseas markets.
Highlighting the company’s export performance, he said Isuzu Motors India has consistently been one of the largest exporters of commercial vehicles from India, he said. The agreement is expected to further strengthen Isuzu’s global supply chain while supporting India’s growing automobile export and maritime logistics ecosystem, he added.
Both KPL and the company did not provide details on the wharfage fee concession.

title: India's exports to UK may reach $115 billion by 2030 due to trade pact: Assocham
content:
UK free trade agreement is expected to boost India's exports to Britain to $115 billion by 2030, industry body Assocham said in a study on Friday.
The agreement came into force on July 15 this year.
"The total trade trajectory is expected to expand from $58 billion in 2025-26 to $115 billion by 2030, along with the possible creation of 7-10 lakh new employment opportunities," it said.
However, the chamber said that for India to realise this massive potential, sustained competitiveness is crucial as Indian businesses will need to meet product quality, certification requirements, Rules of Origin compliance and international sustainability standards.
Ease of doing business reforms and continued investments in infrastructure and supply chain will hold the key to meeting these criteria, Assocham President Nirmal K Minda said.
Minda said that the engineering goods sector is expected to benefit from the agreement, thus providing an impetus for MSME growth and ultimately job creation.

title: Dharmendra Pradhan resigns amid massive student protests, Centre moves to clear Jantar Mantar
content:
UG exam paper leak, Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan said he was stepping down on Saturday and had sent his resignation to Prime Minister Narendra Modi.
Pradhan’s resignation was the primary demand made by youth protesters at the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) protest site at Jantar Mantar in Delhi as well as a precondition for the Congress and other Opposition parties for debating a tough new law against the issue scheduled to be tabled in Parliament on Monday.
Releasing an open letter announcing his resignation in a post on X, Pradhan said he was “saddened by what unfolded over the last 10 days” in reference to protests by students spreading to other cities after taking root a stone’s throw from Parliament at Jantar Mantar.
Soon after Pradhan announced his resignation, security forces started moving into the protest site at Jantar Mantar to evacuate the protestors.
“To ensure that anti-national forces do not exploit the situation arising at Jantar Mantar and across the country, that national unity remains intact, that no student’s future gets tangled in legal complexities, and that our children can focus their time on studying and building their careers—considering all these factors, I have submitted my resignation to the Honorable Prime Minister,” Pradhan said in his letter.
BJP national general secretary organisation BL Santhosh, in a post on X, sought to credit Pradhan for the implementation of the National Education Policy. “Sri @dpradhanbjp as Education Minister successfully oversaw the implementation of NEP 2020. He brought in an over 100 big – small reforms in education field. He had to resign keeping larger social interests in mind. We all are confident of successful future days for him,” he said.
Pradhan’s resignation comes a day after the Union Cabinet approved a draft Bill with provisions for a jail term up to 10 years, penalty up to Rs 10 crore, statutory backing for fast-track courts, and a five-month timeline for investigation and trial of cases.
Story continues below this ad
Here is the full text of the letter
I have been dedicated to students, teachers, and education reform for more than 4 decades. It has always been my conviction that an empowered, inclusive, and forward-looking education system forms the bedrock of an empowered nation.
I deeply respect the aspirations, emotions, and legitimate expectations of the nation’s youth. Fulfilling the dreams of India’s young generation has been the moral resolve of our political and social life. I express my gratitude to the Honorable Prime Minister for the opportunity to serve the nation under his visionary leadership.
However, irregularities came to light during the NEET-UG examination held on May 3, 2026. Taking immediate cognizance, the Government of India handed over the investigation to the CBI, cancelled the exam, and announced a new date. Along with this, a decision was taken to conduct this exam in CBT (Computer-Based Test) mode starting next year.
Story continues below this ad
During this time, our main priority was to ensure that the re-examination for over 20 lakh students was conducted smoothly. For this, work was carried out using a “whole of government approach.” In this, state governments—especially district administrations—played a crucial role alongside the Government of India. With the cooperation of students, guardians, and parents, this exam was completed on June 21, 2026.
From day one, I took responsibility for this and never turned my back on the situation. My resolve was that we would not let any meritorious student’s prospects be ruined by the examination mafia, nor allow injustice to happen to any student.
UG results announced on July 16 were satisfactory, with many meritorious students from underprivileged backgrounds achieving success.
However, during this period, individuals holding responsible positions attempted to create obstacles and mislead several students, which deeply pained my heart.
Story continues below this ad
I have always had unwavering faith in the strength of our democracy and a deep respect for the aspirations, dreams, and expectations of the youth. They are not just India’s future, but the carriers, creators, and architects of a new and developed India (Viksit Bharat).
Looking at the sequence of events over the past 10 days, my heart is deeply distressed. This is not a matter of personal reputation for me.
The youth power of India is the true strength of this country.
My resolve is that we will not let the nation’s youth power fall prey to a web of confusion and misinformation.
Story continues below this ad
national forces do not exploit the situation arising at Jantar Mantar and across the country, that national unity remains intact, that no student’s future gets tangled in legal complexities, and that our children can focus their time on studying and building their careers—considering all these factors, I have submitted my resignation to the Honorable Prime Minister.
I express my heartfelt gratitude to the Honorable Prime Minister for his guidance, trust, and continuous support. Additionally, I extend my thanks to all my esteemed colleagues in the Council of Ministers, ministry officials, staff, and everyone with whom I had the privilege to work. Serving the nation remains the highest priority of my life, and I will always stay dedicated to it.
With the blessings of Lord Shri Jagannath Ji, I will continue to dedicate myself in every possible way to serving Mother India, the people of Odisha, and fulfilling the aspirations of the country’s youth in the future.

title: Anahat Singh first Indian to reach World Junior Squash Championship final since 2005
content:
Anahat Singh has become the first Indian to reach the World Junior Squash Championship final since veteran Joshna Chinappa achieved the feat in 2005.
On Friday (July 24, 2026), the top seeded Delhi girl beat Egyptian 3/4 seed Barb Sameh 11-3 8-11 11-4 11-6 in the semifinals.
World No 20 Anahat, a bronze medal-winning semifinalist last year, is firm favourite, and is just one step away from becoming India's first World Junior squash champion.
"I'm really happy. I played Barb a few months ago at the British Junior Open and it was a close match like this, so I knew I'd have to play really well," Anahat said.
"I didn't play my best yesterday and I knew I had to come out today and show what I'm capable of producing on the court.
"I've played in four World Juniors and lost in the quarters and semis, so reaching the final has made my parents and coaches really happy, but the tournament is not done yet." Anahat will meet Egyptian second seed Ruqayya Salem in the final.

title: Durand Cup | Sahal leads Mohun Bagan to a win over East Bengal
content:

title: Bagan, East Bengal renew rivalry in Durand Cup opener
content:
The new season of Indian football will get underway with the Kolkata derby as Mohun Bagan Super Giant takes on traditional rival East Bengal FC in the Group A fixture of the 135th Durand Cup at the Salt Lake Stadium on Saturday.
Being one of the oldest tournaments in the world, the Durand Cup fittingly begins with the country’s biggest and oldest football rivalry. East Bengal enters the competition as the reigning Indian Super League champion while Bagan, runner-up in the top division last season, will also be eager to make a winning start to its campaign.
East Bengal will be managed by Spaniard Antonio Lopez Habas, who previously guided both Bagan and the erstwhile ATK to ISL titles. Bagan, meanwhile, will begin a new chapter under Greek coach Panagiotis Dilmperis after the 51-year-old’s move from Punjab FC.
The tournament has lost some of its sheen amid uncertainty over the domestic football calendar. With the schedule for the top-flight league yet to be finalised, several ISL clubs have opted to skip the competition. Most participating teams are yet to complete their pre-season preparations, leaving the Durand Cup without a full-strength field despite its status in recent years as the traditional curtain-raiser to the Indian football season.
(The tournament will be shown live on Sony Sports Ten 5, with live streaming available on Sony LIV)

title: World Cup gold-medallist rower fails dope test
content:
In a major embarrassment for Indian rowing, and the Army Rowing Node (ARN) in particular, World Cup gold medallist Lakshay has been provisionally suspended after testing positive in an out-of-competition dope test.
Lakshay, who combined with Ujjwal Singh to win the lightweight double sculls gold at World Cup III in Switzerland last month, tested positive for stanozolol in a sample collected in Pune on May 25.
The triumph was India’s first-ever gold at a rowing World Cup. The result now stands to be annulled if the anti-doping violation is confirmed. The development is also a blow to India’s preparations for this year’s Asian Games, with the Lakshay-Ujjwal combination considered a medal prospect.
The 23-year-old havildar from Haryana had won the lightweight double sculls gold with Ajay Tyagi at last year’s Asian Championships in Vietnam, where he was also part of the silver-winning quadruple sculls team.

title: WATCH: Messi seen for first time since painful World Cup final loss, emerges in Rosario to fans’ cheers
content:
Lionel Messi has made his first public appearance since Argentina's heartbreaking defeat to Spain in the 2026 FIFA World Cup final, with the eight-time Ballon d'Or winner choosing to spend time close to home in Rosario before returning to club football with Inter Miami.
The 39-year-old captained Argentina to a second consecutive World Cup final but was unable to prevent La Albiceleste from losing 1-0 after extra time at New York New Jersey Stadium, where Ferran Torres scored the decisive goal in the 106th minute to hand Spain their second world title.
Messi once again proved central to Argentina's run, finishing the tournament with eight goals and four assists, although he was visibly emotional after the final whistle, leaving the pitch in tears following what is widely expected to have been his final World Cup appearance.
CJP Jantar Mantar Protest Updates
Since then, the Argentina captain has largely stayed out of the public eye. He posted only a brief message on social media after the defeat and did not travel back to Argentina with the rest of Lionel Scaloni's squad, instead returning privately to his hometown of Rosario with his family.
First appearance since the World Cup final
Messi was filmed attending a local football match involving Leones FC, marking his first public appearance since the World Cup final.
Video shared by Argentine outlet Cadena 3 Rosario showed the Inter Miami forward watching the match from a stadium balcony dressed casually in a black hooded sweatshirt and cap. As supporters spotted him and began chanting his name, Messi smiled, waved and acknowledged the crowd before continuing to watch the game.
The broadcaster later wrote on social media that Messi had been in Arroyo Seco to watch Leones FC in action, sharing footage of the Argentine legend greeting supporters during the visit.
Earlier on the same day, other videos circulating on social media showed Messi walking through the streets of Rosario alongside his children. Wearing a hooded jacket and cap, the World Cup-winning captain appeared quiet and reserved, with many supporters noting the contrast between his subdued expression and his usually relaxed demeanour.
Supporting the family's football project
The visit carried extra significance because Leones FC is closely connected to Messi and his family.
Founded in 2015 by the Messi family, the club is chaired by his brother, Matías Messi, and currently competes in Argentina's Primera C, the fourth tier of the country's football pyramid. The team plays its home matches at the Antonio Di Giacomo Stadium in Arroyo Seco, just outside Rosario.
Messi's appearance was widely viewed by Argentine media as a show of support for the family-run project, which has steadily grown since its creation more than a decade ago.
Although the visit attracted considerable attention, it also reflected the forward's preference for spending time with his family in Rosario following one of the most emotionally difficult defeats of his career.
Time to recover before Inter Miami return
Messi is expected to rejoin Inter Miami shortly as the MLS season resumes, although the club is understood to be giving its captain time to recover both physically and mentally after Argentina's demanding World Cup campaign.
The veteran forward carried Argentina throughout much of the tournament, once again demonstrating his enduring quality despite turning 39 during the competition. His performances helped guide the defending champions back to another World Cup final before Spain ultimately ended their title defence through Torres' extra-time winner.
For now, however, football has taken a back seat.
Rather than immediately returning to club duties or media appearances, Messi has chosen the familiarity of Rosario, spending time with his family and supporting a local club that bears his family's imprint before preparing for the next chapter of his career with Inter Miami.

title: Leaked Infantino letter praising Argentina's 'professionalism' emerges amid FIFA probe into World Cup final brawl
content:
up at the 2026 FIFA World Cup has sparked fresh debate after he praised the team's "professionalism" despite football's governing body currently investigating the nation's conduct following the final against Spain.
Spain secured their second men's World Cup title with a 1-0 extra-time victory at the New York New Jersey Stadium after Ferran Torres scored the decisive goal in the 106th minute. While Luis de la Fuente's side celebrated a historic triumph, the final quickly descended into controversy as several Argentina players and members of the coaching staff became involved in post-match confrontations with their Spanish counterparts.
CJP Jantar Mantar Protest Updates
FIFA subsequently opened disciplinary proceedings into the incidents, making the tone of Infantino's private correspondence all the more surprising.
Letter congratulates Argentina despite ongoing investigation
The letter, first reported by Argentine media and later verified by the
Daily Mail, was addressed to Argentine Football Association (AFA) president Claudio "Chiqui" Tapia and formed part of FIFA's customary post-tournament correspondence sent to medal-winning nations.
However, several passages have attracted attention because they commend Argentina's conduct while the federation remains under investigation.
Infantino opened the letter by congratulating Argentina on finishing second at the tournament.
"Dear Mr President, yesterday, Sunday, July 19, 2026, at the magnificent New York New Jersey Stadium, Argentina won the silver medal of the FIFA World Cup 2026 after an exciting final against Spain," he wrote.
"I would like to reiterate my most sincere congratulations for this important new result for Argentine football."
The FIFA president went on to describe the tournament as "an unforgettable celebration of football", highlighting the quality of the matches, emerging young talent, established stars and the atmosphere created by supporters throughout the competition.
He also credited Argentina with playing a significant role in the tournament's success.
"The magnificent performance of the Albiceleste also contributed decisively to making this edition an exceptional event that captivated millions of football enthusiasts around the world."
Praise for 'professionalism' raises eyebrows
Perhaps the most scrutinised section of the letter came when Infantino praised the qualities that he said had underpinned Argentina's run to the final.
He asked Tapia to pass on his congratulations to Lionel Scaloni, the players, coaching staff, medical team and supporters before adding that the achievement reflected "constant work, professionalism and attention to detail," alongside passion, commitment and love for the game.
Infantino concluded by expressing confidence in Argentina's future and wishing the federation success in upcoming competitions before signing off: "With all my friendship, Gianni Infantino."
The correspondence has attracted criticism because it emerged while FIFA continues examining referee reports and video footage relating to the chaotic scenes that unfolded immediately after the final whistle.
World Cup final ended in ugly scenes
Argentina's defeat was followed by confrontations involving several players and members of the coaching staff.
Leandro Paredes appeared to grab Spain defender Eric García by the throat before also clashing with Gavi during the melee, while Nahuel Molina appeared to throw a punch toward Spain captain Rodri. Assistant coach Roberto Ayala and midfielder Thiago Almada have also been linked to the incidents being reviewed.
Much of the Argentina squad also turned their backs as Spain celebrated lifting the World Cup trophy, drawing widespread criticism.
The match itself had already been highly physical. Argentina finished with 10 players after Enzo Fernández was sent off in second-half stoppage time for a second bookable offence following a reckless challenge on Pau Cubarsí, while Spain eventually broke through in extra time when Torres converted Nico Williams' headed knockdown to seal victory.
Controversies extended beyond the final
The final was not the only occasion on which Argentina found themselves at the centre of controversy during the tournament.
Lionel Messi was criticised after appearing to urge Slovenian referee Slavko Vinčić to dismiss Spain defender Marc Cucurella during the final, while Argentina had also faced accusations of simulation and gamesmanship during their semi-final victory over England.
That match generated further headlines after several Argentina players celebrated with a banner reading "Las Malvinas son Argentinas" ("The Falkland Islands are Argentine"), prompting criticism from British political figures and football observers.
Since the final, FIFA has continued its disciplinary investigation into Argentina's conduct, while the wider fallout has intensified.
A petition calling for Argentina to be banned from future World Cups has attracted millions of signatures, while a separate campaign launched by Argentina supporters has demanded the final be replayed over allegations regarding the officiating. However, there is no evidence that FIFA or referee Slavko Vinčić acted improperly during the match, and neither campaign carries any legal or sporting authority over the tournament's result.
Against that backdrop, the emergence of Infantino's congratulatory letter, and particularly its praise for Argentina's "professionalism," has added another layer of scrutiny to FIFA's handling of the aftermath of the 2026 World Cup final, even as its own disciplinary process remains ongoing.

title: 'Don't retire yet': Di María makes desperate plea to Lionel Messi after Argentina's World Cup agony
content:
Ángel Di María has urged Lionel Messi not to retire from international football following Argentina's heartbreaking defeat to Spain in the 2026 FIFA World Cup final, insisting the captain should continue representing his country for "many more years" despite another painful ending on football's biggest stage.
Spain claimed their second men's World Cup title with a 1-0 extra-time victory at the New York New Jersey Stadium after substitute Ferran Torres scored the decisive goal in the 106th minute. The defeat ended Argentina's hopes of retaining the trophy they won in Qatar four years earlier and immediately shifted attention toward Messi's international future.
At 39, Messi has yet to confirm whether he intends to continue playing for Argentina.
CJP Jantar Mantar Protest Updates
While the 2026 tournament is widely expected to have been his final World Cup, his future beyond that remains uncertain.
Di María, who retired from international football after helping Argentina win the 2024 Copa América, believes there should be no pressure on his longtime teammate to step away.
Di María wants Messi to keep playing
Speaking to TNT Sports, Di María said Messi alone should decide when his international career comes to an end.
"Yes, Leo should continue for as long as he wants," Di María said.
"I think he can keep going for many more years."
The former Real Madrid, Paris Saint-Germain and Benfica winger argued that Messi's performances throughout the World Cup proved age has done little to diminish his influence.
"At 39 years old, he's proven he's one of the best and still the best in history, with no ceiling."
Although Argentina ultimately fell short in the final, Messi once again carried much of the creative burden for Lionel Scaloni's side during the tournament.
He finished the World Cup with eight goals and four assists, leading Argentina back to a second consecutive final after inspiring several decisive performances throughout the knockout rounds.
Heartbreak in the final does not define Argentina's campaign
Argentina's title defence came to an end after Torres capitalised in the second period of extra time, shortly after Enzo Fernández had been sent off in stoppage time of normal time following a second yellow card.
Reduced to 10 men, Argentina were unable to find an equaliser as Spain's control of possession eventually translated into the goal that settled the final.
Despite the disappointment, Di María believes the campaign should be remembered for much more than the defeat in New Jersey.
He singled out Argentina's dramatic 2-1 semi-final victory over England as one of the defining moments of the tournament.
"The win over England was a great joy for all of Argentina, and this was clear and made me very happy," he said.
"I am grateful to everyone in the Argentina squad forever."
Reflecting on the team's journey, Di María praised the resilience shown by Scaloni's players throughout the competition.
"I suffered in every match, but the players found the strength within themselves and it led them to victories."
"Sometimes you win finals and sometimes luck is not on your side, but they raised the name of the national team high."
The 38-year-old even suggested that, emotionally, Argentina had already delivered a lasting memory before reaching the final.
"For me, the World Cup ended when Argentina beat England," he said. "They gave the country an indescribable joy."
Di María also backs Scaloni to continue
Messi is not the only senior figure whose future has come under discussion following the tournament.
to-back World Cup titles, but Di María hopes the manager remains in charge to guide the next generation.
"I hope he continues for everyone's benefit, as there is a good generation of young players seeking glory," Di María said.
"He will know what he wants, but I hope he stays."
Argentina head coach Lionel Scaloni leaves the pitch after the World Cup final soccer match between Spain and Argentina in East Rutherford, N.J., near New York, Sunday, July 19, 2026. (AP Photo/Julio Cortez)
Argentina's squad still features a blend of experienced leaders and emerging talent capable of competing for future honours, making continuity an attractive option as preparations eventually begin for the next major international cycle.
Messi yet to reveal his next international decision
Messi has largely stayed out of the spotlight since the final defeat and has not publicly addressed whether he intends to continue playing for Argentina.
His immediate focus is expected to shift back to club football with Inter Miami as the MLS season resumes, while another World Cup appears highly unlikely given his age.
The 2028 Copa América, however, remains a realistic possibility should Messi decide to extend his international career.
For Di María, the message is simple: as long as Messi continues producing performances like those seen throughout the 2026 World Cup, there is no reason to place an artificial deadline on one of the greatest international careers football has ever seen.

title: CWG 2026: Mirabai Chanu leads Manipur’s five-pronged medal charge in weightlifting
content:
As the weightlifting competition at Commonwealth Games begins in Glasgow on Sunday, all eyes will be on
Mirabai Chanu as she takes the platform in the women’s 48kg category, looking to make it three Commonwealth Games titles in a row.
Mirabai has been one of India’s most consistent performers across sports, and the country will be hoping for another memorable display from the Manipuri star as she returns from a career-threatening injury. This time, however, she will not be the state’s only medal hope.
Five members of India’s weightlifting squad hail from Manipur, underlining the state’s remarkable dominance in the sport. Watching their progress with immense pride will be veteran coach S Brojendro Singh, who played a key role in the early development of all five, including Mirabai.
CJP Jantar Mantar Protest Updates
“It’s a matter of great pride for me. I coached all five of them when they first started weightlifting. Seeing them now represent India at the Commonwealth Games is a huge satisfaction,” Brojendro, who has been coaching at the state sports academy since 2004, told STOI.
While Brojendro believes discipline, dedication, sacrifice and unwavering commitment have been central to Manipur’s success in weightlifting, he says Mirabai’s achievements transformed the sport in the state.
“Mirabai inspired an entire generation. After people saw what she achieved, many youngsters took up weightlifting believing they too could reach that level. She showed them that it was possible,” he said.
One of those inspired by Mirabai is Nirupama Devi, the silver medallist at 2025 Commonwealth Championships, who will make her CWG debut in the women’s 63kg category. Although she earned a place in the junior national camp in 2016, thing didn’t go as planned post 2019.
“There were injuries, illness and the Covid-19 break, because of which I was out of national camp. But I kept working hard and now my focus is only on giving my best at CWG,” Nirupama said.
Now training under chief national coach Vijay Sharma at Modinagar, she marked her return with a silver medal-winning total of 217kg at the 2025 Commonwealth Championships. Besides her coaches, Nirupama says Mirabai has also played an important role in her development.
“Mirabai didi always guides us. Whenever we don’t understand something, she patiently explains it and motivates us. She has always been very supportive,” she said.
Another major medal hope is young Martina Devi, who will compete in the women’s +86kg category. After recovering from an ACL injury, she has enjoyed a breakthrough 2026 season, winning both the junior and senior national titles.
Bindyarani Devi, who won silver in the women’s 55kg category at Birmingham CWG, has since moved up to the 58kg division. Rishikanta Singh, who narrowly missed the podium in Birmingham, also changed categories to 60kg and heads into Glasgow after winning gold at the 2025 Commonwealth Championships.
The entire Indian weightlifting squad, meanwhile, completed its final phase of preparations at University of Wolverhampton’s Walsall Campus, where it trained from June 29 until last week before travelling to Glasgow.
The training camp is expected to play a key role as the lifters bid to peak at the right time over the coming days. For Brojendro, however, the medals will tell only part of the story. Watching five lifters who began their journeys under his guidance represent India at the Commonwealth Games is, he says, the greatest reward of his coaching career.

title: Sahal strike gives Mohun Bagan 1-0 win over East Bengal in Durand Cup opener
content:
Mohun Bagan Super Giant began their Durand Cup campaign with a 1-0 win over arch-rivals East Bengal in the opening match of the tournament at the Salt Lake Stadium on Saturday.
Abdul Samad scored the only goal of the match in the 52nd minute, while goalkeeper Vishal Kaith made a series of important saves to help
Mohun Bagan keep a clean sheet.
The decisive moment came after Mohun Bagan pressed high up the pitch. Youngster Kiyan Nassiri won possession near the East Bengal penalty area before driving to the byline and sending the ball across goal. Manvir Singh attempted a backheel but failed to make contact, allowing the ball to roll to Sahal, who slotted it into an open net.
The victory marked a winning start for new Mohun Bagan head coach Panagiotis Dilberis.

His side stayed organised throughout the match, with Kaith leading the defence and Rahul Bheke helping keep East Bengal's attackers quiet.
For East Bengal, it was a losing start under new coach Antonio Habas despite an improved display after the break.
The first half was evenly contested, with Mohun Bagan seeing more of the ball while East Bengal looked to create chances on the counterattack. Neither team managed a clear scoring opportunity before halftime as both defences remained compact.

East Bengal stepped up the pressure in the final 15 minutes and spent long periods in Mohun Bagan's half in search of an equaliser.
Jeakson Singh tried to find P V Vishnu with a long pass from deep, but the ball ran out of play. Soon after, Mohammed Rashid met a loose ball on the edge of the box with a first-time volley, but Deepak Tangri produced a timely sliding block to deny the effort.
East Bengal's best chance came in the 87th minute when Vishnu delivered a cross from the left. Dani Ramirez got a touch at the near post, but the ball struck the outside of the post and went behind.
Kaith then produced the defining save of the match in the second minute of stoppage time. Ramirez floated a cross to the far post where Rashid connected from close range, but Kaith dived to his right to make a point-blank save and seal the win for Mohun Bagan.
The tournament continues on Sunday in Ranchi, where Jamshedpur FC will face defending champions NorthEast United FC in a Group C match.
